hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? was there someone who helped raise you, who didn’t have to?
options: then this story is theirs too. listen.
then you know what this queen did. listen.
that’s okay. listen for the part that helped.

steps.line: Seven days after the prince was born, his mother, Queen Maya, died. Her younger sister, Mahapajapati, took the baby into her arms.
She had a newborn son of her own. The commentaries say she gave him to nurses, and nursed the prince herself, raising him as her own.

steps.q: Years later, she weaves a new cloth with her own hands for the Buddha. What do you think he says?
o: “Thank you, mother. I’ll wear it always.”
“Give it to the whole community instead.”
steps.why: She asks three times, and three times he says: give it to the Sangha, the community of monks. It sounds like a refusal, but he says it will honor him and them both.

steps.line: Years later, after he had become the Buddha, she spun and wove a new cloth herself, and brought it to him. “Please accept this from me.”
“Give it to the community, Gotami,” he said. “Then it honors me and them both.” She asked three times. Three times he said the same.

steps.q: Why turn a mother’s handmade gift toward the whole community?
o: Family ties end once you become a monk
A gift to everyone bears more fruit, and still honors him
A teacher shouldn’t keep anything nice for himself
steps.why: In the same discourse he ranks gifts, and says one given to the whole Sangha is worth more than any gift to a single person, even to a Buddha.

steps.line: Then Ananda spoke up for her. “She is his mother’s sister, his nurse, his foster mother. She fed him when his own mother died.”

steps.q: Later, she asks for something bigger: to become a nun. No woman had ever been ordained. What do you think happens?
o: He agrees the first time she asks
He refuses, and she stays at home
She’s refused, asks again, and wins
steps.why: The Vinaya says she cut her hair, put on robes and walked with other women to ask again, feet swollen. With Ananda’s help, she became the first nun.

steps.line: Later, she asked to become a nun. It took asking more than once, and Ananda’s help again, but she became the first Buddhist nun.

steps.q: In her own verses, kept among the poems of the first nuns, Mahapajapati thanks someone by name for the Buddha. Who?
o: Maya, who gave birth to him
steps.why: “For the good of many, Maya gave birth to Gotama,” she says (Therigatha 6.6). The mother who raised him thanks the mother who bore him.

steps.line: Today, a grandmother does the school run. A stepdad learns to braid hair. Love can be adopted, and it counts.
steps.label: today

say: the buddha’s own discourses say it plainly: seven days after a future buddha is born, his mother dies. no long scene. it adds one line: she reappears in a heaven. a later story tells of him going up to a heaven to teach her.

ananda made sure her care was remembered. in theravada countries the order of nuns that mahapajapati began died out for centuries; since the late 1990s, women have been reviving it, starting in sri lanka. in china, korea, taiwan and vietnam, the line of nuns never broke.

steps.q: The Buddha taught you can’t repay your parents even by carrying them on your shoulders for a hundred years. What did he say does repay them?
o: Giving them wealth and an easy old age
Helping them grow in goodness and wisdom
Honoring them with offerings after death
steps.why: That’s in the Anguttara Nikaya’s book of twos. Helping the woman who raised him to ordain and awaken was, in that light, his way of paying her back.

today.say: today, thank someone who did some of your raising, out loud or in a message: a grandparent, a stepparent, a coach, a neighbor who fed you. the buddha called gratitude rare, the mark of a good person. if it’s complicated, thank the part that helped.
options: they’ll keep it longer than you think.
then thank them quietly. the old texts say the debt is real either way.

tomorrow.title: One finger
tomorrow.line: eight wise men read the baby’s future. seven raise two fingers. the youngest raises one.

Dakkhinavibhanga Sutta (Majjhima Nikaya 142): Mahapajapati offers a pair of new cloths she spun and wove; “give it to the Sangha, Gotami…”; asked three times; Ananda recalls she was his mother’s sister, nurse, foster mother, who gave him milk when his mother died
Commentarial tradition: she gave her own son Nanda to nurses and nursed Siddhattha herself
Vinaya, Cullavagga X.1: her request for ordination, Ananda’s help, the first bhikkhuni; Therigatha 6.6 (her verses)
Anguttara Nikaya 2.32 (mother and father are hard to repay) and 2.118 (the grateful person is rare)
Revival of Theravada bhikkhuni ordination (Sarnath 1996, Bodh Gaya 1998); unbroken Dharmaguptaka lineages in East Asia
